name: EXP-LIFE-002 One commit verb, driven by the git adapter, so delivery and seal stop needing parameters
goal:
EXP-LIFE-002 — One commit verb, driven by the git adapter, so delivery and seal stop needing parameters

OPERATOR REQUEST (2026-10-14, in substance): "I don't want to add a million new verbs all the time...
since we will do an actual integration of the git adapter I think we could drive all that preparation
when committing, so maybe something like `synth expedition consolidate` or `synth expedition commit`
which will do whatever we need to do before any commit, the actual commit, and any post commit stuff
we may like."

PREMISE AND HARD DEPENDENCY: the CLI verbs get fixed FIRST. This expedition depends on EXP-CLI-003
(e47a186cb472a20a), which replaces the 9121-line switch in src/cli/synth.ts with a verb -> loader
registry and enforces a load budget. Adding a verb to the monolith now would mean adding it twice,
and would grow the graph that EXP-CLI-003 exists to shrink. `consolidate` is therefore registered in
the registry, never in the switch. EXP-LIFE-001 (73c5c033360fecf3) is the SOURCE of the findings
below but deliberately not a dependency: it is an audit expedition that may never execute, and
blocking this work on it would block it forever.

THE NAMING CONSTRAINT IS ALREADY BINDING. `synth expedition commit` EXISTS and means something else:
the approved -> committed lifecycle transition (`--proposal-id`, `--all-approved --mission`,
`--branch`, `--no-create`, `--dry-run`; ADR-056 §2.3 forbids two expeditions sharing one branch). It
is not a git commit. So the operator's first-choice name is taken, and taking it anyway would put two
meanings of "commit" one subcommand apart. The verb is `consolidate`. The expedition verb count today
is already 17+ (create, new, approve, commit, start, complete, finish, cancel, archive, delete, move,
evidence, refine, certify, deliver, seal, abandon) — this expedition adds exactly ONE and removes
duplicated commit logic from the others.

WHY: THE DEFECT, MEASURED THIS SESSION
Closing out EXP-CLI-001 (2c13ca22fb8c4e6c) after PR #345 merged required an operator to supply two
parameters the ledger could have derived, and one of them failed:

  * `deliver --branch origin/arena/15e0fc51-synth` returned DELIVERY_PUSH_FAILED: "Could not push
    origin/arena/15e0fc51-synth to origin: Branch origin/arena/15e0fc51-synth does not exist locally
    or on origin" — for a branch `git ls-remote` confirms IS on origin. The verb's default action is
    to PUSH, and `pushBranch` rejects the very `origin/<name>` form that `resolveDeliveryBranch`
    (src/ledger/delivery.ts:254) itself produces while separately computing `canonicalBranch` with the
    prefix stripped. Resolution and pushing disagree about what a branch name is. `--no-push` is the
    documented escape hatch and is what worked.
  * `seal` demanded `--merge-commit <sha>` — a value the operator has to leave the ledger and read off
    GitHub. It is derivable from data the ledger already holds.
  * Neither verb commits. Both wrote canonical-state.json, two event-stream partitions and the
    expedition record, then left the tree dirty for `synth doctor` to report as `ledgerCeremony`.
    Meanwhile `refine`, `start` and `complete` DO auto-commit, each building its own pathspec list —
    which is how commit 5907889 swept 1578 lines of proof/certifications byproduct into history even
    though AUTO_COMMIT_INCLUDE_ROOTS (src/state/artifact-policy.ts:105) says
    [".synth/data", "proof/expeditions", "AGENTS.md"]. Two competing definitions of commit scope, and
    the broader one won. EXP-CLEAN-001 D6(b) records the same leak from the other side; this
    expedition is where it gets fixed, and CLEAN-001's D6 deliverable should be reduced accordingly.

THE INSIGHT THAT MAKES THIS SMALL: seal's only real assertion is CONTAINMENT — "is the work I said I
did actually on main?" — and the ledger already stores the work as a hash
(`metadata.delivery.tipCommit`). Verified against every expedition that has one (4 of 4):

    git merge-base --is-ancestor <tipCommit> main                                  -> containment
    git rev-list --ancestry-path --merges --reverse <tipCommit>..main | head -1    -> the merge commit

  That derivation reproduced, exactly and with no human input, the sha I had looked up on GitHub and
  typed by hand: 2c13ca22 -> 12884da29307 (== the `--merge-commit` supplied manually), 2c9c6c62 ->
  8b8dce269258 (== PR #344's merge), 87e6515d -> 12f1bce56b73, f0f81e35 -> 21ffc64986e6.
  Caveat, stated because it will bite: with stacked merges the derivation returns the FIRST merge
  containing the tip, which can be an intermediate merge rather than the PR merge — f0f81e35 derives
  21ffc64, itself a parent of #343's bb8809ae. Containment is unaffected; only the decorative sha
  differs. `--merge-commit` therefore survives as an optional OVERRIDE, never as a requirement.

THE BACKLOG THIS UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: 34 expeditions are `completed` and only 4 are sealed, so 30 are
completed-but-unsealed. Of those 30, none has a recorded tipCommit (they predate the discipline), so
each needs derivation: 18 can be tied to a merge commit using nothing but main's observable contents
(the PR merge message names the branch, and the branch name carries the expedition id), and 12 cannot
be tied to anything on main at all (e.g. d0a701df55ef36d7, branch
expedition/9861cf62476c90ae/d0a701df55ef36d7) — those are ARCHIVE candidates, not seal candidates,
because there is no evidence their work landed. This supersedes the earlier 24/6 estimate in
EXP-LIFE-001 finding H, which used a looser derivation; under a "justified from main's observable
contents only" rule the honest split is 18/12.

THE SPEC (operator, standing): the no-VCS thought experiment. Any parameter the no-VCS world doesn't
need is a parameter the ledger must not require. In a world without git there is no branch name and no
merge commit — there is only "here is all my work" and "someone with authority accepted it". Measured
against that spec, `deliver --branch` and `seal --merge-commit` both fail today, and `deliver`'s push
fails worst of all: pushing is an ACTION, not an assertion, and it is the one part that broke.

DELIVERABLES
  D1. `synth expedition consolidate` — ONE new verb, three phases, driven through the git adapter:
        PRE     decide what belongs in the commit from ONE authority (the artifact classification in
                src/state/artifact-policy.ts), validate the tree, refuse to sweep byproducts;
        COMMIT  create the commit through `GitRepositoryAdapter` (src/adapters/repository/git.ts:64,
                factory at :747) rather than a fresh child_process git call — this is the "actual
                integration of the git adapter" the operator asked for;
        POST    record the resulting work hash on the expedition, append the ceremony event, and
                report what it compared.
      Support `--dry-run` that is genuinely read-only (unlike `seal --dry-run`, which WRITES —
      EXP-LIFE-001 finding A) and `--message`/`--paths` overrides.
  D2. `consolidate` becomes the SINGLE commit authority. The per-verb auto-commit paths
      (src/ledger/ceremony.ts:339-366 builds its `existing` pathspec list from whatever its caller
      passes; src/ledger/writer.ts:523 likewise) collapse into it. `refine`, `start`, `complete`,
      `finish`, `certify` keep their `--no-auto-commit` opt-out but call the same code. No verb keeps
      a private notion of what a ceremony commit may contain.
  D3. "Here is all my work" is recorded as a hash at commit time, so containment is a comparison
      instead of an archaeology. Every expedition that reaches `completed` carries the tip it was
      completed at.
  D4. `deliver` becomes a pure assertion: no push by default (push becomes opt-in `--push`),
      `--branch` optional (fall back to the recorded execution branch, then the EXPEDITION_BRANCH_CREATED
      event, then a remote ref naming the id — the candidate order `resolveDeliveryBranch` already
      implements), and the record stores the CANONICAL branch name, not a ref path. That fixes
      EXP-LIFE-001 finding G at the source; both existing records (2c13ca22, 2c9c6c62) show the
      `origin/`-prefixed form.
  D5. `seal` requires nothing but `--id`: fetch main (a READ — the only irreducible VCS contact),
      assert containment of the recorded tip, derive and store the integrating merge, and print what
      it compared. If it cannot fetch, it must REFUSE rather than assert — the behaviour I had to
      apply by hand when GitHub was unreachable mid-session. `--merge-commit` stays as an override for
      stacked merges.
  D6. Close the backlog with the derived, guarded procedure: seal the 18 whose integration is
      justified from main's observable contents, archive the 12 that cannot be tied to main, and
      publish both lists with the evidence line for each. No expedition is sealed on a guess.

ACCEPTANCE
  * Exactly one verb is added. `synth expedition --help` lists `consolidate` and still lists
    `commit` with its unchanged lifecycle meaning; the two are documented as different things in the
    help text so the collision cannot confuse the next agent.
  * `synth expedition seal --id <id>` with NO other parameters seals an expedition whose tip is on
    main, and stores a derived merge commit equal to the one an operator would have supplied. Proved
    on a real expedition, not a fixture.
  * `synth expedition deliver --id <id>` with NO other parameters records a delivery, does not push,
    and stores a canonical branch name with no `origin/` prefix.
  * `seal` refuses (non-zero, no write) when main cannot be fetched; proved by breaking connectivity
    or pointing at an unreachable remote.
  * `consolidate --dry-run` writes nothing: tree and event count identical before and after.
  * Commit scope has ONE authority: re-running the 5907889 scenario (a full chain run leaving
    proof/certifications byproducts, then a ceremony commit) stages ledger paths only. A test asserts
    it, chained.
  * All 30 completed-but-unsealed expeditions are resolved: 18 sealed, 12 archived, each with its
    evidence line, and the counts reconciled against the measurement above.
  * `npm run test:all` green with the new tests chained; `synth verify` ok; `synth doctor` 12/12;
    `npm run audit:module-graph` shows the dispatcher graph did NOT grow past EXP-CLI-003's budget —
    the new verb is lazily loaded like every other.
  * EXP-LIFE-001 findings A (seal --dry-run writes), B (deliver needs a durable name), D (seal asserts
    containment unverifiably) and G (ref path vs canonical) are each closed or explicitly re-scoped,
    recorded append-only on that expedition.

NON-GOALS
  * No verb proliferation: one new verb, and no new lifecycle states. If a need appears that seems to
    require a second verb, it is a design failure of this one and gets reported, not built.
  * Not the CLI decomposition or the load budgets (EXP-CLI-003) — this lands on top of its registry.
  * Not dead code, dead imports or the legacy `synth migrate` removal (EXP-CLEAN-001), except that
    CLEAN-001 D6(b)'s ceremony-scope deliverable moves here and CLEAN-001 should be amended to say so.
  * Not the test infrastructure (EXP-TEST-001..005).
  * Not finding J (refinementNote is a single replaced field, so corrections overwrite what they
    correct). It is a real defect and this expedition will keep hitting it — recording findings
    against EXP-LIFE-001 requires the concatenate-don't-replace workaround — but fixing it is a
    separate change to the ledger's write model and stays out of scope here.
  * No network in read paths: `status` and `doctor` stay offline. `consolidate`, `deliver` and `seal`
    may touch the network because they are explicit write actions, and each must say so in its output.

FOLD 2026-10-14 (OPERATOR DECISION) — draft 31a26dadaf47a42d, "Adapter configuration consolidated:
declared vs detected", is folded into this expedition and cancelled as a standalone draft.
============================================================
Reason: it is the same defect class this expedition exists to end — names and configuration carried
forward and acted on without asking the system what is factually true — and it had already diagnosed
today's incident before it happened. Its record is retained (cancelled with a reason, not deleted);
its 4579-char goal stays readable at .synth/data/expeditions/31a26dadaf47a42d.json.

D7 (NEW DELIVERABLE). Adapter configuration has no home: five places, no authority order, no schema.
  (a) .synth/config.yaml holds one `git:` block parsed AD HOC BY THREE INDEPENDENT MODULES
      (ledger/branch.ts:74, adapter/git-snapshot.ts:338, repository/branch-policy.ts) with no type,
      no loader module and no validation, so an unknown or misspelled key is silently ignored.
  (b) `synth init` writes detection results into the generated manifest under
      adapters: {selected, config, diagnostics} (cli/synth.ts:3070-3090) — a regenerable document,
      and absent from this repository's manifest altogether.
  (c) .synth/context.json persists a repository classification (repositoryType, confidence,
      derivedFrom) but no adapter configuration.
  (d) `synth adapter configure repository path=. remote=origin defaultBranch=main promotionMode=direct`
      (cli/adapter.ts:11,74-86) is ACCEPTED AND THEN LOST: GitRepositoryAdapter.configure
      (adapters/repository/git.ts:187-199) merges into in-memory state and never writes, so the verb
      has no durable effect across a process restart.
  (e) Forge credentials are split between env GITHUB_TOKEN and a config schema that declares `token`
      required (adapters/github/adapter.ts:72), which invites a personal access token into tracked YAML.
  Measured consequence, not theoretical: detectRecommendedAdapters already computes defaultBranch and
  remote (cli/detect-adapters.ts:113-119) and BOTH ARE DROPPED, so the same fact is hardcoded three
  times — ledger/delivery.ts:347 defaults baseBranches to ["origin/main","main"] and no caller ever
  passes the option; ledger/branch.ts:49 LEDGER_FALLBACK_BRANCH = "main"; cli/adapter.ts:81
  defaultBranch || "main".

D7 REQUIRED OUTCOMES (from the folded draft, unchanged).
  1. A typed `adapters:` section in .synth/config.yaml — adapters.repository.{provider,remote,
     baseBranch,snapshots,hooks} and adapters.forge.{provider,owner,repo,baseUrl} — read through ONE
     new loader module with schema validation that warns on unknown keys.
  2. Detected observations written to .synth/cache/adapters.json (gitignored, artifact class `cache`
     per state/artifact-policy.ts:58, same precedent as dependency-records.json), each carrying value,
     confidence and derivedFrom, and including a git BINARY probe so that "git is not installed" is
     distinguishable from "git is installed but this directory is not a repository". Today
     first-contact onboard:detect returns byte-identical output for both and advises `synth adapter
     init` even when git is absent — advice the operator cannot follow.
  3. A documented and tested authority order: CLI flag, then config.yaml, then cached detection, then
     built-in default — where the built-in default is provider `none` declaring no capabilities,
     NEVER origin/main.
  4. The three hardcoded branch defaults deleted and fed from configuration through the baseBranches
     option ledger/delivery.ts:347 already accepts.
  5. `synth adapter configure --approve` promotes a detection proposal into config.yaml, plan-then-
     approve in the same shape as first-contact onboard --approve; one mechanism makes the greenfield
     offer and the brownfield offer the same code path.
  6. Credentials resolved from env or a secret store only, with `token` removed from the GitHub
     adapter's required config schema.
  7. The existing `git:` block migrated to adapters.repository.* with a deprecation warning on read,
     and `git.ledgerBranch` RETIRED: the ledger branch inferred from the checkout when it matches
     branchPolicy.declaredPatterns, with trunk as the LAST resort rather than the first.
  8. The ledger-branch fallback order corrected: a checkout matching a declared pattern must win over
     trunk.

OUTCOMES 7 AND 8 ARE NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL — THEY HAPPENED TODAY, ON THIS BRANCH.
  Observed 2026-10-14 while starting EXP-CLI-003: git.ledgerBranch in .synth/config.yaml named
  arena/15e0fc51-synth (the PREVIOUS session's branch, absent from this checkout) and
  .synth/data/ledger.json recorded an even older arena/c5db653e-synth. With both stale, resolution
  fell back to local `main`, exactly as the config comment and the folded draft both predict, so the
  ceremony commits for EXPEDITION_STARTED (23ad2d0c) and EXPEDITION_REFINED (cc669118) were written
  onto the TRUNK and local main diverged from origin/main — by 2 commits then, by 6 earlier in the
  same session (ad7849e, 73d532b, c35bc3e, 915eca0, 62422b9, 26a9997).
  Recovery performed: the ledger content was consolidated onto the session branch (d5c639b), local
  main was reset to origin/main (12884da), and a9cd6e3 set ledgerBranch to arena/d5e4625c-synth —
  which already matches branchPolicy.declaredPatterns ["arena/*"]. That is the WORKAROUND the config
  comment prescribes ("Naming the checkout explicitly is the current workaround"), not the fix: the
  key is still session-scoped inside tracked config and is stale by construction the moment a session
  ends. Outcomes 7 and 8 are the fix, and this expedition now owns them.

ORDERING INSIDE THIS EXPEDITION. D7 is a PREREQUISITE for D1, not a parallel item. D1 drives the
  commit path through GitRepositoryAdapter, but outcome (d) above shows the adapter cannot durably
  hold configuration today — configure() merges in memory and never writes. Consolidating
  configuration and giving the adapter a durable, typed home must land before the commit path is
  routed through it, or the new verb inherits the same silent-fallback behaviour.
  Cross-link: EXP-CLEAN-001 D6(b) wants ONE authority for what a ceremony commit may CONTAIN; D7
  wants ONE authority for WHICH BRANCH it lands on and where configuration comes from. Same
  single-authority theme, different axis — coordinate so the two do not each grow a private resolver.

SCOPE EXTENSION REQUIRED. `expedition refine` cannot change scope, so this must be applied when the

  (Current scope already covers src/cli/**, src/ledger/**, src/adapters/repository/**, src/infra/**,
  tests/**, data/tasks/**, docs/adr/**, AGENTS.md.)

ACCEPTANCE ADDED FROM THE FOLDED DRAFT.
  * The three-system matrix — no git at all / git installed without a repository / git installed with
    a repository — yields distinct, truthful recognition output and identical ledger behaviour in all
    three.
  * No repository or branch value is hardcoded outside the loader's documented defaults; the three
    hardcoded branch defaults are gone.
  * `synth adapter configure` survives a process restart.
  * No secret can be written into .synth/config.yaml.
  * The ledger records ceremonies with zero VCS present, reporting verification as UNAVAILABLE rather
    than failing.
  * A ceremony commit lands on the checkout that matches branchPolicy.declaredPatterns, never on
    trunk, with no session-scoped branch name stored in tracked config.

============================================================
MEASURED EVIDENCE 2026-10-14 — a verb created and checked out a branch it was told not to create,
and the ledger recorded a branch name that exists nowhere
============================================================
Observed while starting EXP-CLI-003 (e47a186cb472a20a) on this session branch. Reproduced, then
diagnosed from code and event offsets rather than inferred.

WHAT RAN
  synth expedition commit --proposal-id e47a186cb472a20a --branch arena/d5e4625c-synth --no-create
  -> rc=0, and its own output reported executionBranch {"branch":"arena/d5e4625c-synth","created":false}
  -> the reflog simultaneously recorded: "checkout: moving from arena/d5e4625c-synth to
     expedition/framework-maturation-v2-4ab7e9d/exp-cli-003-make-the-light-path-light-and-enforce-the-load-budgets-e47a186"
  The output contradicted the reflog. Both were telling the truth about different code paths.

TWO INDEPENDENT BRANCH PATHS INSIDE ONE VERB
  Path A — ADR-056 declaration, src/repository/branch-declaration.ts:92-112. Reads --branch and
    --no-create. Because currentBranch already equalled the declared branch it did nothing, and
    emitted event 485 EXPEDITION_BRANCH_BOUND {branch: arena/d5e4625c-synth, created: false,
    baseCommit: 189f7029ac21}. Correct.
  Path B — the ECOSYSTEM-001 canonical-branch auto-create, src/cli/synth.ts ~6552-6599, INSIDE
    cmdExpeditionCommit (which spans 6423..6923). Its own comment says "Auto-create the canonical
    expedition branch at start... When it runs, it switches to the canonical branch". It computes
    canonical = candidates[0] and calls adapter.branchExists / adapter.checkout(canonical) /
    adapter.createBranch(canonical). IT NEVER READS noCreate OR declaredBranch; its only guards are
    policy.mode === "enforce" && policy.strategy === "featured" and whether the current branch is
    already a canonical candidate. It emitted event 486 EXPEDITION_BRANCH_CREATED for the canonical
    name at the same baseCommit.
  Events 485 and 486 are adjacent offsets, which is what proves both paths fired in one invocation
  rather than the creation coming from a later command.

CONSEQUENCE: A SELF-INFLICTED DEADLOCK
  The ledger then bound execution to arena/d5e4625c-synth (Path A) while the checkout stood on the
  canonical branch (Path B). The next `expedition start` failed BRANCH_POLICY_DENIED: "expedition
  execution is bound to arena/d5e4625c-synth (ADR-056); current branch is expedition/framework-...
  Required branch: arena/d5e4625c-synth" — denying the transition because the verb had itself moved
  the checkout off the branch the ledger declared.
  Operator note, recorded honestly: the SECOND creation (event 487) was my error, not the framework's
  — I ran `expedition start --id e47a186c` bare, although ADR-056 §2.1 documents
  `expedition start --id ... --branch <name>` and cmdExpeditionStart does read flags.branch and
  flags["no-create"]. Run correctly, `start --id e47a186cb472a20a --branch arena/d5e4625c-synth
  --no-create` returned ok with executionBranch {created: false, declared: true}, did NOT switch
  branches, did NOT create anything, emitted event 488 EXPEDITION_BRANCH_BOUND, and moved the
  expedition to executing (autoCommit 23ad2d0c). So the deadlock is escapable — but only by an
  operator who knows to repeat the declaration on a second verb, after the first verb already
  ignored it once.

A BRANCH NAME RECORDED THAT EXISTS NOWHERE
  The canonical name is derived by slugifying mission + subject + id8
  (canonicalBranchCandidates, src/repository/branch-taxonomy.ts:133) and then materialized to make
  the derivation true. It was recorded twice (events 486 and 487, baseCommits 189f7029ac21 and
  1423d53d6611). It was never pushed: `git ls-remote --heads origin | grep -c exp-cli-003` = 0. It no
  longer exists locally (deleted twice during recovery). And the expedition record itself never
  mentions it — 0 occurrences of the string in .synth/data/expeditions/e47a186cb472a20a.json — so the
  contradiction lives only in the event stream, where nothing reconciles BOUND against CREATED.
  This is the operator's diagnosis confirmed: the branch layer GUESSES names from strings and creates
  reality to match, instead of asking git what exists. The hash layer is the only factual part, which
  is exactly why containment-by-tipCommit worked for 4 of 4 sealed expeditions while every
  name-based path in this session either failed (DELIVERY_PUSH_FAILED) or needed a human to go read
  GitHub (--merge-commit).

WHAT THIS EXPEDITION MUST THEREFORE DO, BEYOND ITS ORIGINAL DELIVERABLES
  * One authority for branch decisions. A verb must not contain two paths that can disagree; if a
    declared branch exists, the canonical auto-create path must not run, and `--no-create` must bind
    every path in the verb, not just the one that implements it.
  * A verb's output must describe what it DID, not what one of its paths intended. Returning
    created:false while a checkout happened is worse than either behaviour alone, because it sends
    the operator looking for the wrong cause.
  * Never record a branch name that was not verified to exist, and never leave BOUND and CREATED
    events unreconciled. If a name is derived, either verify it against git or do not write it.
  * Declaration must not have to be repeated per verb. `--branch`/`--no-create` given at commit time
    is already in the ledger (EXPEDITION_BRANCH_BOUND); `start` should read that binding instead of
    requiring the operator to restate it, and should refuse to switch away from a bound branch.
Sequencing per operator instruction 2026-10-14: 'Draft the expedition with the premise that we will fix the CLI verbs before.' EXP-CLI-003 replaces the 9121-line switch with a verb -> loader registry, so 'consolidate' is registered there rather than added to the monolith and then moved. EXP-LIFE-001 (73c5c033360fecf3) is the source of findings A, B, D, G, H and J used in this goal but is deliberately NOT a dependency: it is an audit expedition that may never execute, and blocking on it would block this work indefinitely.
